title: NEET UG 2026 - Set 2: High Probability (Most Repeated Patterns)
description: 180 MCQs focusing on topics that appeared in EVERY single year (2020-2024). These are near-certain to appear again based on 5-year consistency analysis.

deep_analysis.methodology: Topics that appeared in ALL 5 years (2020-2024) with frequency ≥ 2 questions per year
physics_guaranteed_topics: Kirchhoff's Laws / Circuit Analysis (every year, 2-3 Q)
Electromagnetic Induction & AC Circuits (every year, 2-3 Q)
Modern Physics: Photoelectric + de Broglie + Radioactivity (every year, 3-4 Q)
Electrostatics: Coulomb's Law + Capacitors (every year, 2-3 Q)
Optics: Young's DSE + Refraction + Lenses (every year, 2-3 Q)
Kinematics: Projectile + Relative Motion (every year, 1-2 Q)
Rotational Motion: MOI + Rolling (every year, 2 Q)
Thermodynamics: PV diagrams + KTG (every year, 2 Q)
chemistry_guaranteed_topics: Coordination Compounds: IUPAC + CFT + Magnetism (every year, 2-3 Q)
Organic Named Reactions + Mechanisms (every year, 3-4 Q)
Chemical Kinetics: Rate Law + Arrhenius (every year, 2 Q)
Chemical Bonding: Hybridization + VSEPR (every year, 2 Q)
Solutions: Raoult's Law + Colligative Properties (every year, 1-2 Q)
Solid State: Unit Cell + Packing (every year, 1-2 Q)
biology_guaranteed_topics: Genetics: Mendelian + Pedigree + Chromosomal (every year, 4-5 Q)
Molecular Biology: DNA Replication + Transcription + Translation (every year, 4-5 Q)
Ecology: Succession + Population + Biodiversity (every year, 4-5 Q)
Cell Biology: Cell Cycle + Organelles (every year, 3-4 Q)
Human Physiology: Digestion + Respiration + Excretion (every year, 5-6 Q)
Plant Physiology: Photosynthesis + Transpiration (every year, 3-4 Q)
Biotechnology: rDNA + PCR + Applications (every year, 3-4 Q)
Animal Classification: Phyla + Match-the-column (every year, 3-4 Q)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the circuit shown, a 12V battery with internal resistance 2Ω is connected to three resistors of 4Ω, 6Ω, and 12Ω in parallel. The current drawn from the battery is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The terminal potential difference of a cell of EMF 6V and internal resistance 1Ω when it sends a current of 2A through an external circuit is:
questions.explanation: V = EMF - Ir = 6 - 2×1 = 4V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A potentiometer wire of length 100 cm has a resistance of 10Ω. It is connected in series with a resistance of 40Ω and a battery of EMF 2V. The potential gradient along the potentiometer wire is:
questions.explanation: Current = 2/50 = 0.04A. Potential across wire = 0.04 × 10 = 0.4V. Gradient = 0.4/100 = 0.004 V/cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A circular coil of radius 10 cm and 50 turns is rotated about its vertical diameter with an angular speed of 100 rad/s in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.03 T. The maximum EMF induced in the coil is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an AC circuit, the voltage applied is E = E₀sin(ωt). The resulting current is I = I₀sin(ωt - π/2). The power consumed in the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Power = E_rms × I_rms × cos(φ). Phase difference = π/2, so cos(π/2) = 0. Power = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the resistance, inductance and capacitance are 20V, 30V and 15V respectively. The applied voltage is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At resonance in a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the capacitor is:
questions.explanation: At resonance, Q-factor amplifies voltage. V_C = QV (where Q = ωL/R). Since Q > 1 typically, V_C > V_applied.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work function of a metal is 4.2 eV. If radiation of wavelength 200 nm is incident on the surface, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is: (hc = 1240 eV·nm)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 100V is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive element is 30 minutes. The fraction of initial activity remaining after 2 hours is:
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives = 120/30 = 4. Fraction = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In hydrogen atom, the ratio of energies of the electron in 2nd and 4th orbits is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical conducting spheres carrying charges of 6μC and -2μC are brought into contact and then separated. The charge on each sphere after contact is:
questions.explanation: Total charge = 6 + (-2) = 4μC. After contact, each gets 4/2 = 2μC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance 6μF is charged to a potential of 100V. The energy stored in it is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric flux through a closed surface enclosing charge q is given by φ = q/ε₀. If the charge is doubled and the radius of the Gaussian surface is halved, the flux becomes:
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, flux depends only on enclosed charge, not on surface size. φ = 2q/ε₀

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is β. If the entire setup is immersed in a liquid of refractive index μ, the fringe width becomes:
questions.explanation: Wavelength in medium = λ/μ. Fringe width = λD/d. New fringe width = β/μ

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 40 cm. The power of the combination is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The critical angle for a medium of refractive index √2 is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball is projected at an angle of 60° with the horizontal with a speed of 20 m/s. The time of flight is: (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower 80 m high. At the same time, another stone is projected upward from the base with a velocity of 40 m/s. They will meet after: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Relative velocity of approach = 40 m/s (relative acceleration = 0). Time = 80/40 = 2s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder of mass M and radius R about its axis is MR²/2. If it rolls without slipping, the ratio of rotational KE to total KE is:
questions.explanation: For rolling: KE_rot/KE_total = (½Iω²)/(½mv² + ½Iω²) = (I)/(mR² + I) = (MR²/2)/(MR² + MR²/2) = 1/3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A disc of mass M and radius R is rotating about its axis with angular velocity ω. If a small mass m is gently placed on its rim, the new angular velocity is:
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂. (MR²/2)ω = (MR²/2 + mR²)ω'. ω' = Mω/(M+2m)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal expansion from volume V to 2V. The work done by the gas is:
questions.explanation: For isothermal process: W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = nRT ln(2V/V) = nRT ln2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio Cp/Cv for a monoatomic ideal gas is:
questions.explanation: For monoatomic gas: Cv = 3R/2, Cp = 5R/2. γ = Cp/Cv = 5/3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The average kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas at temperature T is:
questions.explanation: Average KE = (3/2)kT for any ideal gas molecule (translational).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a full-wave rectifier, if the input frequency is 50 Hz, the output frequency is:
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectifier output frequency = 2 × input frequency = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a p-n junction diode, the barrier potential depends on:
options: Nature of semiconductor material and doping concentration
questions.explanation: Barrier potential depends on the semiconductor material (Si ~0.7V, Ge ~0.3V) and doping concentration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long straight wire carrying current I produces a magnetic field B at a distance r from it. If the current is doubled and distance is halved, the new magnetic field is:
questions.explanation: B = μ₀I/2πr. New B = μ₀(2I)/2π(r/2) = 4 × μ₀I/2πr = 4B

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle moving with velocity v enters a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to it. The radius of the circular path is:
questions.explanation: Lorentz force provides centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r. Therefore r = mv/qB

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle executes SHM with amplitude A. At what displacement from the mean position is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy?
questions.explanation: KE = PE means ½mω²(A²-x²) = ½mω²x². So A² = 2x². x = A/√2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The time period of a simple pendulum is T. If its length is increased by 44%, the new time period is:
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L. New L = 1.44L. New T = T√1.44 = 1.2T

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from Earth is v. The escape velocity from a planet with mass 4 times and radius 4 times that of Earth is:
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R). New v = √(2G×4M/4R) = √(2GM/R) = v

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The value of acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the radius of Earth is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between the slits is 0.5 mm and the screen is 1 m away. If the wavelength of light used is 500 nm, the fringe width is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an electromagnetic wave, the electric and magnetic fields are:
options: Perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation
Perpendicular to each other but parallel to direction of propagation
questions.explanation: EM waves are transverse. E and B are mutually perpendicular and both perpendicular to direction of propagation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant is the same as that of:
questions.explanation: h has dimensions [ML²T⁻¹]. Angular momentum (L = mvr) also has dimensions [ML²T⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body of mass 2 kg moving with velocity 4 m/s collides with another body of mass 1 kg at rest. If the collision is perfectly inelastic, the loss in kinetic energy is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Water flows through a horizontal pipe whose cross-section is not uniform. The pressure is 30000 Pa at a point where the velocity is 4 m/s. The pressure at another point where velocity is 6 m/s is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work done in blowing a soap bubble of radius R is W. The additional work required to increase its radius to 2R is:
questions.explanation: W = 8πR²T (two surfaces). Additional work = 8π(2R)²T - 8πR²T = 32πR²T - 8πR²T = 24πR²T = 3W

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The magnetic susceptibility of a paramagnetic material is 10⁻⁴. Its relative permeability is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei with mass number around:
questions.explanation: Fe-56 has the maximum binding energy per nucleon (~8.8 MeV), making it the most stable nucleus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency band used for TV broadcast is:
questions.explanation: TV broadcasts use VHF (Very High Frequency: 30-300 MHz) and UHF (Ultra High Frequency: 300 MHz-3 GHz).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The threshold frequency for a metal surface is ν₀. When light of frequency 2ν₀ is incident on it, the maximum velocity of photoelectrons is v. When light of frequency 5ν₀ is incident, the maximum velocity is:
questions.explanation: ½mv² = h(2ν₀) - hν₀ = hν₀. For 5ν₀: ½mv'² = h(5ν₀) - hν₀ = 4hν₀ = 4(½mv²). v' = 2v

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three capacitors of capacitances 2μF, 3μF and 6μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The speed of a transverse wave on a string of mass 0.01 kg and length 2 m, when tension in the string is 8 N, is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A block of mass 10 kg is placed on a rough inclined plane of inclination 30°. If the coefficient of friction is 1/√3, the force required to just move the block up the incline is: (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl is:
questions.explanation: Ligands in alphabetical order: ammine before chlorido. Metal: cobalt(III). Counter ion: chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of unpaired electrons in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is:
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ has d⁶ configuration. CN⁻ is strong field ligand → pairing occurs. t₂g⁶ eg⁰ → 0 unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following complex ions shows geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is octahedral with formula [MA₄B₂] which shows cis-trans isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The major product of dehydration of 2-methylbutan-2-ol is:
questions.explanation: By Saytzeff's rule, the more substituted alkene is the major product. 2-methylbut-2-ene (trisubstituted) is preferred.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Grignard reagent reacts with formaldehyde to give:
questions.explanation: RMgX + HCHO → RCH₂OH (primary alcohol after hydrolysis)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following reactions is an example of nucleophilic addition?
questions.explanation: HCN addition to acetone (C=O) is a classic nucleophilic addition reaction on carbonyl group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aldol condensation is given by:
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation requires α-hydrogen. Acetaldehyde has α-H atoms and readily undergoes aldol condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The standard electrode potential of Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34V and Zn²⁺/Zn is -0.76V. The EMF of a Daniel cell is:
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The molar conductivity of 0.025 M acetic acid is 11.2 S cm² mol⁻¹. If the limiting molar conductivity is 390.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, the degree of dissociation is approximately:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a first-order reaction, the time required for 99% completion is how many times the time required for 90% completion?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature increases from 300K to 310K. The activation energy of the reaction is approximately: (R = 8.314 J/mol/K)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following oxides of nitrogen is a brown gas?
questions.explanation: NO₂ (nitrogen dioxide) is a brown/reddish-brown gas. It is a pungent smelling gas responsible for smog.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of acidic strength of oxyacids of chlorine is:
questions.explanation: Acidic strength increases with the number of oxygen atoms (more electronegative atoms stabilize conjugate base). HClO < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hybridization of the central atom in SF₆ is:
questions.explanation: S in SF₆ forms 6 bonds with 6 F atoms. It requires 6 hybrid orbitals → sp³d² hybridization.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the following, which molecule has the shortest bond length?
questions.explanation: N₂ has a triple bond (N≡N) with bond order 3, giving it the shortest bond length (1.10 Å) among these.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The boiling point elevation of a solution containing 3g of a non-volatile solute in 100g of water is 0.15°C. The molecular weight of the solute is: (Kb = 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For an ideal solution, the value of enthalpy of mixing (ΔH_mix) is:
questions.explanation: For ideal solutions, ΔH_mix = 0 and ΔV_mix = 0 (Raoult's law is obeyed).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of atoms per unit cell in a body-centered cubic (BCC) structure is:
questions.explanation: BCC: 8 corners × 1/8 + 1 center = 1 + 1 = 2 atoms per unit cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The packing efficiency of a face-centered cubic unit cell is approximately:
questions.explanation: FCC packing efficiency = (4 × 4πr³/3)/(16√2 r³) × 100 = π/(3√2) × 100 ≈ 74%

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a spontaneous process at constant temperature and pressure:
questions.explanation: The criterion for spontaneity at constant T and P is ΔG < 0 (Gibbs free energy decreases).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), the relationship between ΔH and ΔU is:
questions.explanation: ΔH = ΔU + ΔnRT. Δn = 2 - (1+3) = -2. ΔH = ΔU + (-2)RT = ΔU - 2RT

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following transition metal ions is colourless?
questions.explanation: Zn²⁺ has completely filled d-orbitals (d¹⁰), so no d-d transition is possible → colourless.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The highest oxidation state of manganese is found in:
questions.explanation: In KMnO₄, Mn is in +7 oxidation state (the highest for Mn). MnO₂ has +4, MnSO₄ has +2, Mn₂O₃ has +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Nylon-66 is an example of:
questions.explanation: Nylon-66 is formed by condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, with loss of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The amino acid which is not optically active is:
questions.explanation: Glycine (H₂N-CH₂-COOH) has no chiral center (two H atoms on α-carbon), so it's optically inactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following does not give iodoform test?
questions.explanation: Iodoform test requires CH₃CO- or CH₃CH(OH)- group. Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) lacks these groups.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of SN1 reactivity is:
questions.explanation: SN1 depends on carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl. (CH₃)₃C⁺ is most stable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tyndall effect is shown by:
questions.explanation: Tyndall effect (scattering of light) is characteristic of colloidal solutions due to particle size (1-100 nm).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pH of 0.01 M NaOH solution is:
questions.explanation: NaOH is a strong base. [OH⁻] = 0.01M. pOH = 2. pH = 14 - 2 = 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The buffer solution is prepared by mixing:
options: Weak acid and its salt with strong base
questions.explanation: Buffer = weak acid + salt of weak acid with strong base (e.g., CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Lucas test is used to distinguish between:
questions.explanation: Lucas test (ZnCl₂/conc. HCl) distinguishes 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols by different rates of turbidity appearance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hofmann's bromamide reaction converts:
options: Amide to primary amine with one less carbon
questions.explanation: RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O. Product has one less carbon atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct stability order of carbocations is:
questions.explanation: Carbocation stability: resonance stabilized > 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl. Triphenylmethyl is most stable due to extensive resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the extraction of aluminium, the role of cryolite is to:
options: Lower the melting point of alumina
questions.explanation: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) lowers the melting point of Al₂O₃ from 2050°C to about 950°C for electrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Li has the highest reduction potential (most negative E°) due to high hydration enthalpy despite small size → strongest reducing agent in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Photochemical smog is formed by the combination of:
options: NOₓ, hydrocarbons, and O₃ in sunlight
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog results from NOₓ and hydrocarbons reacting in sunlight to produce ozone, PAN, and other oxidants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Heavy water is:
questions.explanation: Heavy water is deuterium oxide (D₂O), where D is the isotope of hydrogen with mass number 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The strongest acid among the following is:
questions.explanation: More electronegative groups (Cl) increase acidity by -I effect. CCl₃COOH has 3 Cl atoms → strongest acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The shape of ClF₃ molecule is:
questions.explanation: ClF₃: Cl has 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = sp³d hybridization. Due to lone pairs in equatorial positions, shape is T-shaped.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction: 2FeCl₃ + SnCl₂ → 2FeCl₂ + SnCl₄, the reducing agent is:
questions.explanation: Sn²⁺ → Sn⁴⁺ (loses electrons = oxidized). The species that gets oxidized is the reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The maximum number of electrons in a subshell with l = 3 is:
questions.explanation: l = 3 is f-subshell. Maximum electrons = 2(2l+1) = 2(7) = 14.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The unit of rate constant for a zero-order reaction is:
questions.explanation: For zero-order: rate = k. Units of k = units of rate = mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Wurtz reaction is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Wurtz reaction: 2RX + 2Na → R-R + 2NaX. It gives higher symmetrical alkanes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Faraday's first law of electrolysis states that the amount of substance deposited is proportional to:
questions.explanation: m = ZQ = ZIt. Mass deposited is directly proportional to quantity of electricity (charge) passed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of structural isomers possible for C₄H₁₀O that are alcohols is:
questions.explanation: C₄H₁₀O alcohols: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol = 4 isomers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a cross between two tall pea plants, the ratio of tall to dwarf in the offspring is 3:1. The genotypes of both parents are:
questions.explanation: 3:1 ratio (phenotypic) is obtained only from a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt × Tt).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a dihybrid cross, the ratio of offspring showing both dominant traits to those showing both recessive traits is:
questions.explanation: In 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio, 9/16 show both dominant traits and 1/16 show both recessive. Ratio = 9:1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A colour-blind man marries a woman who is a carrier for colour blindness. The probability of their son being colour-blind is:
questions.explanation: Father X^c Y × Mother X^C X^c. Sons get X from mother: X^C (normal) or X^c (colour-blind). Probability = 50%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Down's syndrome is caused by:
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome = Trisomy 21 (2n = 47). Extra copy of chromosome 21 due to non-disjunction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that unwinds DNA during replication is:
questions.explanation: Helicase unwinds the double-stranded DNA by breaking hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Okazaki fragments are formed on:
questions.explanation: Okazaki fragments are short DNA segments formed on the lagging strand because DNA polymerase synthesizes only in 5'→3' direction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the sequence of one strand of DNA is 5'-ATGCTTGA-3', the sequence of the mRNA transcribed from the complementary strand is:
questions.explanation: Template strand is 3'-TACGAACT-5'. mRNA (5'→3') = AUGCUUGA (same as coding strand with U replacing T).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The central dogma of molecular biology is:
questions.explanation: Central dogma: DNA (replication) → RNA (transcription) → Protein (translation). Proposed by Francis Crick.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pyramid of energy in an ecosystem is always:
questions.explanation: Pyramid of energy is always upright because energy decreases at successive trophic levels (10% rule).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ecological succession on a bare rock is called:
questions.explanation: Xerosere is the succession on bare rock (xeric habitat). It starts with crustose lichens as pioneer community.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a food chain, the amount of energy available decreases at each trophic level. This is called:
questions.explanation: Lindeman's 10% law states only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biodiversity is richest in:
questions.explanation: Tropical rain forests have the highest biodiversity due to favorable climate, high productivity, and evolutionary time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organelle called 'suicidal bags' of the cell are:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes. If membrane ruptures, the enzymes digest the cell (autolysis) → suicidal bags.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell organelle involved in the formation of the cell plate during plant cell division is:
questions.explanation: Golgi apparatus produces vesicles that fuse at the equator to form the cell plate during cytokinesis in plant cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The number of chromosomes in a human cell during G2 phase of cell cycle is:
questions.explanation: G2 is after S phase (DNA replication). Chromosome number remains 46 but each has two sister chromatids (4n DNA content).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Tidal volume of air in a normal healthy person is approximately:
questions.explanation: Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during normal breathing, approximately 500 mL.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pacemaker of the heart is:
questions.explanation: SA node (sino-atrial node) generates impulses at the highest rate (70-75/min) and sets the pace of heartbeat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Bowman's capsule and glomerulus together form:
questions.explanation: Malpighian corpuscle (renal corpuscle) = Bowman's capsule + Glomerulus. It is the site of ultrafiltration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone stimulates glycogenolysis in the liver?
questions.explanation: Glucagon (from α-cells of islets of Langerhans) stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis to raise blood glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach at pH:
questions.explanation: Pepsin is optimally active at pH 1.5-2.5 (highly acidic). HCl in stomach provides this acidic environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first stable product of C₃ cycle (Calvin cycle) is:
questions.explanation: In C₃ plants, CO₂ fixation by RuBisCO produces 3-PGA (3-carbon compound) as the first stable product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Kranz anatomy is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Kranz anatomy (wreath-like arrangement of bundle sheath cells) is found in C₄ plants like maize, sugarcane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The site of photolysis of water during photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water (H₂O → 2H⁺ + ½O₂ + 2e⁻) occurs in PS II located in the grana thylakoid membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme used to join two DNA fragments is:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds. It seals the 'nicks' in the sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is used as a vector in rDNA technology?
questions.explanation: pBR322 is a plasmid cloning vector with ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes and multiple restriction sites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In PCR, the step that involves separation of two DNA strands by heating is called:
questions.explanation: Denaturation step (94-98°C) breaks hydrogen bonds between complementary strands to separate double-stranded DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bt cotton is resistant to:
questions.explanation: Bt cotton has cry gene from Bacillus thuringiensis that produces crystal protein toxic to bollworm (insect pest).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of formation of sperms from spermatogonia is called:
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis is the complete process of sperm formation from spermatogonia through meiosis and differentiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Double fertilization in angiosperms involves fusion of:
options: One sperm with egg + one sperm with polar nuclei
questions.explanation: Double fertilization: one sperm + egg → zygote (2n), other sperm + 2 polar nuclei → Primary Endosperm Nucleus (3n).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of hormonal secretion during menstrual cycle is:
questions.explanation: FSH from pituitary → follicle growth → Estrogen from follicle → LH surge → ovulation → corpus luteum → Progesterone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: Mammary glands are the defining feature of mammals. They produce milk for nourishing the young ones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungi belong to the kingdom:
questions.explanation: In five-kingdom classification (Whittaker), Fungi is a separate kingdom. They are heterotrophic, eukaryotic organisms with cell walls of chitin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The characteristic feature of phylum Arthropoda is:
questions.explanation: Arthropoda (largest phylum) is characterized by jointed appendages, chitinous exoskeleton, and segmented body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The phenomenon of industrial melanism is an example of:
questions.explanation: Industrial melanism in peppered moths shows natural selection: dark moths survived better on soot-darkened trees during industrialization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Homologous organs indicate:
questions.explanation: Homologous organs (same origin, different function) indicate divergent evolution from a common ancestor (e.g., forelimbs of vertebrates).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The causative organism of malaria that causes malignant tertian malaria is:
questions.explanation: P. falciparum causes malignant (cerebral) tertian malaria with 48-hour cycle. It is the most dangerous species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Widal test is used for the diagnosis of:
questions.explanation: Widal test detects antibodies against Salmonella typhi antigens (O and H) in blood serum → diagnosis of typhoid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pneumatophores are found in:
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores are aerial roots growing vertically upward in mangrove plants (Rhizophora) for gaseous exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Placentation in which ovules develop on the central axis is called:
questions.explanation: Axile placentation: ovules attached to a central axis of an ovary with septa (e.g., tomato, lemon).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The secondary structure of protein is stabilized by:
questions.explanation: Secondary structure (α-helix, β-pleated sheet) is stabilized by hydrogen bonds between C=O and N-H groups of backbone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of starch to maltose is:
questions.explanation: Amylase (salivary/pancreatic) hydrolyzes starch into maltose by breaking α-1,4-glycosidic bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Crossing over occurs during which stage of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Crossing over (exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids) occurs at pachytene stage of prophase I.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The significance of meiosis is:
options: It produces genetic variation in gametes
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces haploid gametes with genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Erythropoietin is produced by:
questions.explanation: Erythropoietin (EPO) is produced by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney in response to hypoxia, stimulating RBC production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The nerve that controls the diaphragm during breathing is:
questions.explanation: Phrenic nerve (from cervical spinal nerves C3-C5) innervates the diaphragm and controls its contraction during breathing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between:
questions.explanation: Mycorrhiza is a mutualistic association between fungal hyphae and plant roots. Fungi absorb water/minerals; plant provides organic food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cyanobacteria are classified under:
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are prokaryotes → Kingdom Monera. They have chlorophyll a and perform oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plant hormone primarily responsible for apical dominance is:
questions.explanation: Auxin (produced at shoot apex) inhibits growth of lateral buds, causing apical dominance. Removing apex promotes branching.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transpiration pull is based on the property of water called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration pull works due to cohesion (water molecules attract each other) and adhesion, creating continuous water column (cohesion-tension theory).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The greenhouse gases include:
questions.explanation: Major greenhouse gases: CO₂ (60%), CH₄ (20%), N₂O, CFCs. They trap infrared radiation causing global warming.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the ovule that develops into the seed coat after fertilization is:
questions.explanation: Integuments of the ovule develop into the seed coat (testa and tegmen) after fertilization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In vitro fertilization (IVF) involves:
options: Fertilization outside the body followed by embryo transfer
questions.explanation: IVF: ova and sperm are collected and fertilized in lab (in vitro). The resulting embryo is transferred to the uterus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Polygenic inheritance is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Polygenic traits (skin color, height) show continuous variation. Multiple genes contribute additively → bell-shaped (normal) distribution curve.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the genetic code?
questions.explanation: The genetic code is non-overlapping (each nucleotide is part of only one codon). It IS universal, degenerate, and unambiguous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Golden rice is enriched with:
questions.explanation: Golden rice has been genetically engineered to produce beta-carotene (provitamin A) in the endosperm to combat Vitamin A deficiency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The promoter region of a prokaryotic gene has the consensus sequence:
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic promoter has Pribnow box (TATAAT) at -10 position and -35 region. RNA polymerase binds here to initiate transcription.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In lac operon, the inducer molecule is:
questions.explanation: Allolactose (an isomer of lactose) is the true inducer of lac operon. It binds to repressor, causing it to release from operator.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Myelin sheath is formed by:
questions.explanation: Schwann cells form myelin sheath in PNS; oligodendrocytes in CNS. Myelin provides insulation for faster nerve conduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ADH (Antidiuretic hormone) is secreted by:
options: Hypothalamus (synthesized but released from posterior pituitary)
questions.explanation: ADH is synthesized in hypothalamus but stored and released from posterior pituitary. It promotes water reabsorption in collecting ducts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term 'biodiversity' was popularized by:
questions.explanation: Edward O. Wilson popularized the term 'biodiversity' through his 1988 publication. He is called the 'Father of Biodiversity'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The 9+2 arrangement of microtubules is found in:
questions.explanation: Axoneme of cilia and flagella has 9+2 arrangement (9 peripheral doublets + 2 central singlets). Centriole has 9+0 (9 triplets).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cork cambium (phellogen) forms:
options: Cork (phellem) towards outside and secondary cortex (phelloderm) towards inside
questions.explanation: Phellogen cuts off phellem (cork) towards outside and phelloderm (secondary cortex) towards inside. Together they form periderm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Collenchyma provides:
options: Flexibility and mechanical support to growing organs
questions.explanation: Collenchyma has thickened corners (pectin), provides mechanical support with flexibility to growing plant organs (stems, petioles).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of stages of spermatogenesis is:
options: Spermatogonia → Primary spermatocyte → Secondary spermatocyte → Spermatid → Sperm
questions.explanation: Spermatogonia (2n) → mitosis → Primary spermatocyte (2n) → meiosis I → Secondary spermatocyte (n) → meiosis II → Spermatid (n) → spermiogenesis → Sperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The species-area relationship is given by the equation:
options: log S = log C + Z log A
questions.explanation: Species-Area relationship (Alexander von Humboldt): log S = log C + Z log A, where S = species richness, A = area, Z = slope (regression coefficient).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A test cross is a cross between:
options: F₁ hybrid and homozygous recessive parent
questions.explanation: Test cross: crossing an organism with unknown genotype with homozygous recessive (tt). It reveals if the organism is homozygous or heterozygous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The movement of phloem sap is explained by:
questions.explanation: Munch's pressure flow hypothesis: sucrose loading at source creates high osmotic pressure, driving mass flow to sink through phloem sieve tubes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bile juice does not contain any digestive enzyme but aids digestion by:
questions.explanation: Bile salts emulsify fats (break large fat droplets into smaller ones), increasing surface area for lipase action.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Henle's loop is important for:
questions.explanation: Loop of Henle creates a concentration gradient in medulla via counter-current mechanism, enabling concentration of urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The anticodon of tRNA that recognizes the codon AUG is:
questions.explanation: Anticodon is complementary and antiparallel to codon. AUG → anticodon 3'-UAC-5' (written as UAC).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The geological era in which dinosaurs were dominant is:
questions.explanation: Mesozoic era (Age of Reptiles): 250-65 million years ago. Dinosaurs dominated during Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium requires:
options: No mutation, no selection, random mating, large population, no gene flow
questions.explanation: HW equilibrium conditions: no mutation, no natural selection, random mating, large population size, no migration (gene flow).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ELISA test is based on the principle of:
questions.explanation: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) uses antigen-antibody reaction with enzyme-linked detection for diagnosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a parasitic food chain, the pyramid of numbers is:
questions.explanation: In parasitic food chain: Tree → Birds → Parasites → Hyperparasites. Numbers increase → inverted pyramid of numbers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell theory was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Cell theory was proposed by Schleiden (1838, plants) and Schwann (1839, animals). Virchow added 'Omnis cellula-e-cellula' later.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood group determination is an example of:
questions.explanation: ABO blood groups show codominance: alleles I^A and I^B are both expressed in blood group AB individuals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Corpus luteum secretes:
questions.explanation: Corpus luteum (formed from ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation) secretes primarily progesterone, maintaining pregnancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Heterospory is found in:
questions.explanation: Selaginella (pteridophyte) produces two types of spores: microspores (male) and megaspores (female) → heterosporous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water vascular system is characteristic of phylum:
questions.explanation: Water vascular system (ambulacral system) is unique to echinoderms. Used for locomotion, food capture, and respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an autoimmune disease?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks the body's own joint tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Abscisic acid is called stress hormone because:
options: It increases the tolerance of plants to various stresses
questions.explanation: ABA accumulates during water stress, causes stomatal closure, inhibits growth, and promotes dormancy → called stress hormone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The concept of ecological niche was given by:
questions.explanation: Charles Elton (1927) introduced the concept of ecological niche (the functional role of an organism in its community).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which RNA has clover-leaf structure?
questions.explanation: tRNA has a characteristic 2D clover-leaf structure with acceptor arm, anticodon loop, D-arm, and TψC arm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Law of independent assortment is applicable to genes located on:
questions.explanation: Independent assortment occurs when genes are on different (non-homologous) chromosomes. Linked genes on same chromosome don't assort independently.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with:
questions.explanation: RER has ribosomes on its surface for protein synthesis. These proteins are then processed and transported.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hormone responsible for 'fight or flight' response is:
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from adrenal medulla prepares the body for emergency: increases heart rate, BP, blood sugar, dilates bronchioles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Placenta produces which of the following hormones?
questions.explanation: Placenta produces hCG (maintains corpus luteum), hPL (growth hormone-like), estrogen, progesterone, and relaxin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Restriction enzymes are also called 'molecular scissors' because they:
options: Cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific recognition sequences (palindromes), producing fragments for cloning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The interaction where one species is benefited and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is:
questions.explanation: Commensalism (+/0): one benefits, other unaffected. E.g., epiphytes on trees, barnacles on whales.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of air passage in respiratory system is:
options: Nostrils → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli
Nostrils → Larynx → Pharynx → Trachea → Bronchioles → Bronchi → Alveoli
Nostrils → Pharynx → Trachea → Larynx → Bronchi → Alveoli
questions.explanation: Air pathway: External nostrils → nasal chamber → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
